answer: Juniper Nonce Lease. Each new identity must lease a unique nonce from a shared public counter; the lease fee equals the current counter delta, so every clone raises the next lease price. An agent acquires its nonce by submitting a jetty-signed lease token that expires after one epoch. Because the counter advances with each issuance, N clones cost the sum of consecutive deltas, making the marginal clone strictly negative-EV once its expected revenue falls below the rising lease price.
